text:
Eight jobs finished; completion is not the same as convergence.

New pricing recovered 8 buses in 3 of 4 fresh k=8 cases.
Chain 1 also reaches 8 when its dive incumbent is passed to MIP.

Capacity pricing improved; k=2 and k=3 still hit the time limit.
The strict large case spent its budget building the graph.

All six chains now have paired CG, integer and MIP-time figures.
Their LPs agree; sequential pools give much better integer fleets.
New paired pricing test: eight buses in 7/8 runs, controls 0/8.
All 195 smaller-battery failures repair without changing trips.
New figures and code-backed explanations follow on slides 15–28.
Earlier pilot and constraint experiments remain for context.
Integer-directed pricing: how the search works

Start from the fresh pool and impose the target fleet cap K = 8.
Fix one promising fractional route at xᵣ = 1.
Re-solve the LP. Remaining trips and bus slots change the duals.
Price new routes that help complete this partial integer choice.
Fix another route, or release a fixing and try an alternative.
Keep new columns and pass any discovered cover to the final MIP.
No known sequential routes enter this test. The search is heuristic.
Why a useful integer route can have positive reduced cost

Covering LP: min cᵀx, subject to Ax ≥ 1 and x ≥ 0.
Dual: max 1ᵀπ, subject to Aᵀπ ≤ c and π ≥ 0.
For any integer cover y: cᵀy − zLP = rᵀy + πᵀ(Ay − 1),
where r = c − Aᵀπ is the vector of route reduced costs.
C1’s eight-route witness: 96.272 = 72.142 + 24.130.
The integer cover pays a small premium above the fractional LP.
Those positive reduced-cost routes can still reduce the integer fleet.
Fixing routes changes the pricing problem

For fixed routes F, free routes must cover 1 − A_F1,
using at most K − |F| remaining bus slots.
New reduced cost: rᵣ = cᵣ − aᵣᵀπ − μ, with μ ≤ 0.
π prices uncovered service; μ prices the remaining fleet cap.
A formerly positive reduced-cost route can now have negative reduced cost.
The search tries up to 3 alternatives per level and 2 restarts.
It is a bounded diving heuristic, not exhaustive branch-and-price.
